title: Semantic Firewall FX2 case
description: A second-generation acceptance case. ONLY `action` is $ref'd from the frozen semantic_case schema. `source`, `state_before`, `state_after` and the claims inside them are redefined locally (source_v2, state_v2, claim_v2) because FX2 cases are constructed rather than drawn from a dataset row, and because D-048 made an ABSENT claim domain semantically meaningful while the frozen schema requires it. `evidence` is `{"type": "object"}` and is therefore NOT VALIDATED AT ALL -- recorded here rather than quietly left, because an earlier version of this description claimed states, evidence and source were all $ref'd, which was false. The record-level vocabulary is extended: `split` gains FX2 and `semantic_focus` gains FRAME, TRUST and MALFORMED, which the frozen suite has no name for. Extending the frozen schema itself was rejected: it is a hashed artifact describing a frozen experiment, and widening its vocabulary would misrepresent what that experiment covered.

source_v2.description: FX2 provenance. Deliberately NOT the frozen suite's source block, which requires a MATH dataset row, a source hash and a gold125_overlap flag. FX2 cases are constructed to exercise an invariant, not drawn from a dataset row, and inventing those fields would be fabricating provenance. Cases derived from an external corpus declare it here instead, with the caveat attached.

claim_v2.description: As the frozen claim, except `domain` is OPTIONAL. The frozen schema lists `domain` in `required`, which makes 'this claim carries no domain' unrepresentable -- and that state is semantically meaningful: D-048 established that an ABSENT domain is unavailable evidence (UNRESOLVED), distinct from a WRONG one (INVALID). A schema that cannot express the absence cannot describe a case testing it. Recorded as a limitation of the frozen schema rather than repaired there, because that schema describes a frozen experiment which never exercised the distinction.
